subject: Dedicated capacity: guardrails for slot reservations & burst policy
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: guardrails for slot reservations & burst policy

Team —

Helium Health is asking for a guaranteed reserved lane for their Q1 pilot (they're asking to reserve 12 GPUs equivalent for 6 weeks), plus the ability to burst beyond the reservation in a predictable way. Before I respond, I want to align on what guardrails we can offer without creating downstream capacity debt. High level asks:

- Can we offer a time-boxed reservation (start 2027-01-10) with a clear burst policy (how much, how long, and SLO impact)?
- What approvals are needed from infra/ops for an exception to autoscaling limits?
- Any pricing/discount constraints that sales should flag?

I've attached the Helium MAP spreadsheet they shared. tagging Rishi & Hannah for ops constraints, Lauren for product signal, Dev for commercial terms, and Markus for model-sensitivity notes.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: guardrails for slot reservations & burst policy

Naomi —

Quick technical constraints from infra: we can carve a 12-GPU equivalent reservation if the pools are available, but two important caveats:

1) Autoscaling exceptions: our current autoscaler has a hard safety cap (for shared pools) to prevent noisy neighbors. To allow bursts beyond reservation we need an "exception flag" that routes traffic to a dedicated burst lane (isolated nodes) — that requires an ops ticket and a 48–72 hour lead time to provision during Q1.

2) Burst economics & throttling: we should define burst windows (max 4 hours/day, max 24 hours/week) and a soft-reroute policy to cheaper variants once sustained >75% utilization for 12 hours. Otherwise we risk impacting committed SLA customers.

I'll attach a small CSV with expected infra delta if we allow the burst (estimated extra vGPU hours).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
[attachment: prod-infra-delta.csv (csv, 18KB)]

Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: guardrails for slot reservations & burst policy

Thanks, Naomi + Rishi. A few product considerations:

- Helium's pilot is latency-sensitive for ER docs ingestion; they need headroom for episodic inference spikes during data loads. 
- We should offer a formal "burst profile" (e.g., +30% for short windows) plus a hard cap that triggers a fallback to a quantized model variant to preserve latency SLOs.
- Timeline: product prefers that any exception be limited to a single sprint provisioning window and include automatic rollback rules.

If we expose burst controls to customers, we must also expose the expected cost delta (so Dev can price it).

I can draft a short playbook blurb describing behavioral expectations and the automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: guardrails for slot reservations & burst policy

Folks —

Operational process and approvals:

- Approval path: infra (Rishi) -> ops lead (me) -> revenue ops for pricing exception -> infra provisioning. Revenue ops sign-off typically takes 24–48 hours if there is a documented cost fallback.
- Provisioning lead time: 72 hours during Q1 peak. If Helium needs a guaranteed start date we should provision in the dedicated pool and mark it as "pilot-reserved" in the console.
- Exception rules we can enforce at provisioning time: burst window limits (configurable), automated fallback (model variant), and per-day overage caps billing to Helium's account.

I've uploaded a slot-reservation proposal that includes the configuration knobs we use in staging (burst max/min, fallback threshold). Suggest we mirror that to a customer-facing doc with clear billing language.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Ops Manager, Dedicated Capacity
[attachment: slot-reservation-proposal.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: guardrails for slot reservations & burst policy

Rachel —

Thanks for the details and sample timelines. We can support a 6-week pilot starting 2027-01-10 with the following guardrails (internal summary below and PDF attached):

1) Reservation: 12 GPU-equivalent reserved lane for 2027-01-10 through 2027-02-20.
2) Burst policy: up to +30% sustained for 4 hours/day, max 24 hours/week. Sustained use beyond those windows triggers an automatic fallback to a quantized model variant and overage billing as per the attached proposal.
3) Provisioning: provisioning lead time is 72 hours; to guarantee the start date please confirm by 2026-12-29.
4) Pricing: Dev will send a short addendum with the pilot pricing (includes an overage rate).

Next steps: Rachel, please confirm approval on the timeline and we will route the provisioning ticket. Dev — can you prepare the pilot addendum and a concise pricing table?

Cheers,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
